newsitem.title: BELGIUM: British schoolboys hurt in Belgian coach attack.
newsitem.headline: British schoolboys hurt in Belgian coach attack.

text.p: Two British schoolboys were injured when their coach was hit by concrete blocks thrown from a motorway bridge near Liege, eastern Belgium, early on Saturday, police said.
The boys, both aged 14, were in one of two British coaches returning from a trip to Germany and were taken to hospital after the attack at about 0530 local time (0330 GMT).
British officials named them as Ross Jelf from West Bromwich in central England and Richard Comery from nearby Great Barr.
Jelf was the more seriously hurt of the two but his life was not in danger, the officials said. The boys' families were on their way to Belgium to see them in hospital in Liege.
